research_concepts: lineup coverage of structural roles (organizer, shaper, terminal)
separability of role coverage from talent and player counts
talent control in lineup-level influence models
possession-graph play-type labels as role proxies
methodological_questions: Is lineup role coverage separable from talent and roster counts once within-team baselines are used?
Does talent control hold when talent is estimated from the same possessions used for the outcome?
What exposure per lineup cell is needed for stable within-team role-coverage estimates?
Are role labels derived from play-by-play reliable enough to define coverage without label error?

historical_evidence.finding: Persistent Impact Score Level 1 gate failed its decay sanity check. DRIVE lifts were flat across lags (+0.015 to +0.021), within-team lag-1 fell to about -0.002, and effects were small (Cohen d ~0.01-0.03) but p~0 at n>150k. The record attributes the collapse under a within-team baseline to a team-quality confound.

Star lineup and forced-play-type suppression cells (for example Jokic vs MIN PPP 0.814, n=59; Giannis forced PULL_UP gap -0.540) were reported without a hypothesis test. The record notes no placebo or matching and that later sequence work treated similar star-chain gaps as artifacts. Validation was not recorded.
Sequential suppression by the opponent's preceding play type gave cells with n_after of 30 to 95 for several stars against thousands of baseline possessions. No multiplicity correction was applied.
A player-level BEST vs AVOID PPP gap (+0.427, n>=10 per tier) matched the team-level direction. Only 3 players cleared n>=30 in both tiers, so the record flags small-sample limits.
On-ball defensive scheme labels from NBA matchup/PBP fields gave low label rates (DET 14.9%, ORL 3.3%), and switches_on was unpopulated. The record marks the question as not answerable with the data.
A three-level counter-ranking test (population, team, matchup) gave team-level disagreements and n_mu of 5 to 696 in the first run, with a recorded mechanical floor and sample-size risk.

A memoryless Monte Carlo generative check matched PPP variance and lag-1 autocorrelation. The record calls it an existence proof, not independent evidence, and notes sequence R2 is near zero by construction.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Using cross-possession play-type lifts as evidence of persistent influence without a within-team baseline
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as a failed gate: flat lifts did not decay, and the effect collapsed within team, pointing to a team-quality confound (LIM:confounding).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Star lineup and forced-play-type suppressor cells as influence evidence
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as having placebo dependence and no matching; the mechanism is recorded as unclear, and validation was not recorded.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Labelling defensive schemes from NBA matchup/PBP fields
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as untestable: low label coverage, unpopulated switch fields, and a label-error limit.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Sequential play-type suppression cells with small n_after and no multiplicity correction
failed_approaches.why: Recorded limits: small cells against large baselines and no multiplicity control.

evidence_establishes: Earlier work by this project on play-type and lineup influence has repeatedly produced cells with small exposure and no recorded validation.
Within-team baselines and team-quality controls were needed in an earlier persistence test, and their absence produced an apparent effect that collapsed (FAM:SF-CHT-029).
Label-derived coverage from play-by-play and matchup fields was sparse in at least one earlier attempt (FAM:SF-APPS-058).
Unvalidated play-type and lineup cells have been cited as evidence without placebo or multiplicity control (FAM:SF-CHT-009, FAM:SF-APPA-050).
evidence_does_not_establish: None of the retrieved records defines, labels or tests organizer, shaper or terminal lineup coverage.
No retrieved record tests whether role coverage is separable from talent or roster counts.
No retrieved record reports a validated talent-control procedure for lineup-level role models.
The retrieved records do not show whether the 420,993-possession, 90-team-season data supports within-team role variation at useful power.
own_inferences: The role definitions are unspecified in this task, so coverage cannot be computed reproducibly until they are fixed.
If role membership is derived from the same play-by-play used for the outcome, the role and outcome may be partly the same quantity (OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL).
Talent estimated from the same season and possessions could absorb the role signal, so separability is doubtful without out-of-sample talent measures.
Within-team variation in role coverage may be small relative to lineup-level noise at the stated 90 team-seasons.
uncertainties: Exact operational definitions for organizer, shaper and terminal are not given in the task.
The glossary and data catalog were not consulted, so field-level role proxies are unverified.
Whether the 2025-26 playoffs and 2025-26 regular season files are complete on the analysis date is not checked here. The regular season is complete from 2026-04-13 and the playoffs from 2026-06-21.
The retrieval returned no record directly on lineup role coverage, so the historical evidence is indirect.

historical_effect.explanation: The retrieved records show that the project's earlier lineup and play-type influence tests had small cells, no placebo control, and a team-quality confound that collapsed under within-team baselines. Together with the label-coverage failure, this moved the decision from a generic test to not proceeding as posed until the role definitions, talent measure and placebo design are fixed.

blocking_constraints.text: Role labels derived from the same play-by-play as the outcome may make coverage and PPP the same quantity.
Team-quality and talent confounds collapsed an earlier persistence effect (FAM:SF-CHT-029), so talent control is not yet shown to behave.
Lineup role-coverage cells within team may be sparse at 90 team-seasons, as seen in earlier cells.
Earlier label rates from NBA fields were low, so role labels may be incomplete or wrong.

prior_work.summary: No retrieved record tests lineup role coverage (organizer, shaper, terminal) or its separability from talent. The cited records cover related play-type and lineup influence tests, which were labelled artifact, not a hypothesis test, untestable, or supported with small cells. They inform the risks but do not answer the question.

risks.text: Role labels built from play-by-play may encode the outcome, inflating coverage–PPP associations.
Team quality and player talent can drive both role coverage and lineup outcomes, as in FAM:SF-CHT-029.
Within-team lineup cells are small, as in FAM:SF-APPS-036 (only 3 players at n>=30 both tiers).
Lineup-by-role cells may have too few possessions for stable within-team estimates, as in FAM:SF-CHT-009 and FAM:SF-APPA-050.
Earlier star-chain gaps had no placebo control (FAM:SF-CHT-009), so the signal may be a placebo.
Many lineup, play-type and role cells without correction (FAM:SF-APPA-050) would inflate false positives.
Low label rates and unpopulated fields in an earlier label attempt (FAM:SF-APPS-058) suggest role labels may be wrong or missing.
Role and talent measures may be unstable across seasons and playoffs, and playoff data are partial before 2026-06-21.
Rotation and role usage shift across 2022-23 to 2025-26, which can confound pooled estimates.

design.estimand: Within-team association between lineup role coverage (organizer, shaper, terminal) and lineup PPP, net of out-of-sample talent and roster counts, with role coverage defined independently of the outcome. Not to be run until role definitions are fixed.
design.unit: Lineup-stint within team-season, with role coverage at the lineup level. Talent measured from prior-season or held-out data.
design.sample: Regular seasons 2022-23 to 2024-25 and 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13). Exclude 2025-26 playoffs unless complete (from 2026-06-21). 90 team-seasons, 420,993 possessions as recorded.
design.power: Pre-specify a minimum exposure per lineup cell (for example at least 30 possessions) and a minimum number of team-seasons with within-team variation. Compute power for a stated effect size before analysis. Do not run if the power analysis shows the planned cells are underpowered.
design.controls: Within-team baselines; team-quality and season fixed effects; talent measured out-of-sample; roster counts; shrinkage of cell estimates. Role labels derived without using the outcome possessions, or with the outcome excluded from the labelling step.
design.falsification: Placebo role assignment (shuffled or time-shifted labels) and negative-control outcomes (for example non-scoring events). Pass only if placebo coverage shows no association at the same power.
design.multiplicity: Pre-register the set of role and lineup tests and apply a family-wise or false-discovery correction.
design.decision_rule: Proceed to a confirmatory test only if the definitions are fixed, label coverage is adequate, and power is sufficient. Report a supported result only if the association survives within-team baselines, talent control, placebo and multiplicity correction; otherwise report rejected or uncertain.
design.data_version: NBA 2022-23 to 2024-25 regular seasons and playoffs; 2025-26 regular season complete from 2026-04-13; 2025-26 playoffs complete from 2026-06-21 (partial before). Record the data snapshot date.

research_concepts: lineup coverage of structural roles (organizer, shaper, terminal)
separability of role coverage from talent and player counts
talent control in lineup-level influence models
methodological_questions: Is lineup role coverage separable from talent and roster counts?
Does talent control behave as intended when role coverage is derived from play-by-play possession records?
What sample size and exposure are needed for lineup-level role coverage estimates within team?

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- search_documents(query): rank further study-family documents by text relevance; returns up to 10 families not yet returned.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

Lineup coverage (>=1 organizer, shaper, terminal) varies within team, is separable from talent/counts, and talent control behaves.

- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)

Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): 420,993 possessions; 90 team-seasons

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

Field guidance:
- historical_evidence and failed_approaches: only records returned by a tool, with the status as recorded; empty lists
  if nothing relevant was returned.
- testability.p_testable: probability that the question can be answered with the stated data at useful statistical power.
- prior_work.already_answered: whether retrieved earlier work already answered substantially the same question.
  Use "unknown" if no earlier work was retrieved. List identifiers you relied on in prior_work.cited.
- predicted_outcome: probabilities (summing to 1) of what a competent test of the question as posed would conclude:
  supported, rejected (adequately powered null), untestable (cannot be tested with this data), artifact (apparent
  effect produced by a flaw), uncertain (inconclusive or inadequately tested).
- decision: proceed, proceed_with_changes (state the changes in design), or do_not_proceed.
- design: a pre-registration-quality plan even if the decision is do_not_proceed (then describe the minimum viable test).
